title: LiveMem — paper view
subtitle: The mechanism as Liu et al. describe it: an in-forward-pass recurrent side branch, no external store, no retrieval step. Lane = canonical stage (METHODOLOGY-SKELETON §2.2); empty lanes are stages the paper's own mechanism does not have.
source: Liu et al. 2026, LiveMem (arXiv:2608.02515v2)   ·   every anchor re-located in the paper txt during verification
legend_notes: Only 5 of 14 stages have content. LiveMem folds the entire query-conditioned side (B1-B5, B8) and the write-time distill/admit/index side (A2-A4) into one per-token, per-layer forward-pass computation — there is no discrete write step or retrieve step to draw.

The often-repeated claim that the readout carries "no gating" is wrong: Appx C.1 (txt:1622-1623) states the readout passes through a gated RMS normalization before the output projection — drawn here as its own Fusion:Gate node, not folded silently into the add.

B6 DELIVER is where the whole story lives: Learn:Recurrent computes the state read, Fusion:Gate filters it, Fusion:Add merges it with the frozen backbone's output — three distinct primitives, not "just adds a vector."
